# Objects distinguished by the runtime

The robjc runtime determines whether a value is a class generator, a protocol generator, or a class instance.
These checks support factory argument validation, inheritance checks, collection elements, and archive restoration.
This note (03) explains the predicates in `R/runtime_robjc.r` and the S3 classes on which they rely.
See [note 01](tech_01_isa.Rmd) for the structure of `isa` itself.

## Three kinds of object

Both an R6 class generator and an instance returned by `$new()` are environments.
`is.environment()` cannot distinguish them.
An ordinary R6 generator and a robjc generator are also alike in this respect.
robjc marks generators and `isa` records with S3 classes, while instances carry a private reference to `.__isa`.

```{r}
library(robjc)

PlainR6 <- R6::R6Class("Tech03PlainR6")
Example <- RSObjectClass("Tech03Example")
instance <- Example$new()
Protocol <- RSProtocolClass("Tech03Protocol", contract_methods = "run")

stopifnot(is.environment(PlainR6))
stopifnot(is.environment(Example))
stopifnot(is.environment(instance))
stopifnot(is.environment(Protocol))
```

## `class(isa)` and `class(self)`

Each class definition has an `isa` metadata environment.
An object class's `isa` has the S3 classes `RSObjectIsA` and `RSIsA`; a protocol's `isa` has `RSProtocolIsA` and `RSIsA`.
An instance's `class(self)` contains class names from the current class up through its parents.
The same `class()` function therefore describes different kinds of environments.

```{r}
stopifnot(identical(class(Example$robjc_isa), c("RSObjectIsA", "RSIsA")))
stopifnot(identical(class(Protocol$robjc_isa), c("RSProtocolIsA", "RSIsA")))
stopifnot(identical(class(instance), c("Tech03Example", "RSObject")))
stopifnot(identical(instance$class(), Example))
```

The distinction is also visible inside a method through `self` and `private$.__isa`.
`self$class()` returns the generator stored in `private$.__isa$class`, rather than searching the strings in `class(self)`.

```{r}
Inspect <- RSObjectClass("Tech03Inspect",
  public = list(
    inspectClasses = function() list(
      instance = class(self),
      isa = class(private$.__isa)
    )
  )
)
view <- Inspect$new()$inspectClasses()
stopifnot(identical(view$instance, c("Tech03Inspect", "RSObject")))
stopifnot(identical(view$isa, c("RSObjectIsA", "RSIsA")))
```

## Generator markers

An ordinary object class generator has `RobjcClass` and `R6ClassGenerator` markers.
A Singleton generator additionally has `RobjcSingleton`.
That marker is a property of an object class, not a fourth object category.
Protocol generators also carry `RobjcClass`, so their generator S3 class alone does not distinguish them from object classes.
The runtime also inspects `RSObjectIsA` or `RSProtocolIsA` on `isa`.

| Target | Main evidence |
|:--|:--|
| Object class generator | Environment, `RobjcClass`, and `RSObjectIsA` on `isa` |
| Singleton generator | Object class conditions plus `RobjcSingleton` |
| Protocol generator | Environment, `RobjcClass`, and `RSProtocolIsA` on `isa` |
| Instance | Environment with private `.__isa` marked `RSObjectIsA` |

## `robjc_isMetaClass()`, `robjc_isClass()`, and `robjc_isProtocol()`

`robjc_isMetaClass()` requires an environment marked `RobjcClass` whose `robjc_isa` carries `RSIsA`.
Despite the name, this predicate accepts **both** object class and protocol generators.
`robjc_isClass()` further requires `RSObjectIsA`.
`robjc_isProtocol()` instead requires `RSProtocolIsA`.

```{r}
stopifnot(robjc_isMetaClass(Example), robjc_isClass(Example))
stopifnot(robjc_isMetaClass(Protocol), robjc_isProtocol(Protocol))
stopifnot(!robjc_isClass(Protocol), !robjc_isProtocol(Example))
stopifnot(!robjc_isMetaClass(PlainR6))
```

## `robjc_isInstance()`

An instance is not a generator and holds its class's `isa` at `.__enclos_env__$private$.__isa`.
`robjc_isInstance()` checks that the value is an environment without the generator marker, then checks for a private environment and an `.__isa` marked `RSObjectIsA`.
It does not rely on the strings in `class(instance)` alone.

```{r}
lookalike <- structure(new.env(), class = "Tech03Example")
stopifnot(robjc_isInstance(instance))
stopifnot(!robjc_isInstance(Example))
stopifnot(!robjc_isInstance(PlainR6$new()))
stopifnot(!robjc_isInstance(lookalike))
```

This predicate recognizes objects produced through ordinary robjc construction; it is not a security boundary against deliberately forged environments.
A caller that reproduces the internal markers can reach the limits of a marker-based check.

## `robjc_isRObjC()` and choosing a predicate

`robjc_isRObjC()` returns true when either `robjc_isMetaClass()` or `robjc_isInstance()` does.
It suits an entry point that accepts classes, protocols, and instances.
An `isa` record is internal robjc metadata but is not itself accepted by this predicate.

```{r}
stopifnot(robjc_isRObjC(Example))
stopifnot(robjc_isRObjC(Protocol))
stopifnot(robjc_isRObjC(instance))
stopifnot(!robjc_isRObjC(Example$robjc_isa))
```

| Accepted value | Predicate |
|:--|:--|
| Object class or protocol generator | `robjc_isMetaClass()` |
| Object class generator | `robjc_isClass()` |
| Protocol generator | `robjc_isProtocol()` |
| Class instance | `robjc_isInstance()` |
| Any of those generators or an instance | `robjc_isRObjC()` |

After classifying a value, use `robjc_inheritChain()` or an instance's `isKindOf()` to inspect inheritance.
Keeping classification separate from inheritance lets the runtime work with generator references instead of relying solely on class-name strings.
